title: Traffic siphon and KV reconciliation hotpatch for cross-region relay incidents
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a partial cross-region network partition we observed sustained elevated error rates for a subset of tenants routed through the us-east relay tier. Root cause appears to be a subtle KV cache divergence combined with an aggressive routing policy that overloaded warm standbys. This ticket captures a hotpatch runbook to siphon traffic away from degraded relays, run a targeted KV reconciliation, and restore steady-state with minimal customer impact. Deliverables: (1) executable playbook for SRE/Oncall, (2) a scoped code patch to throttle relay ingress for affected relays, (3) validation checks and dashboards to confirm KV alignment, (4) customer comms templates and postmortem stub.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook executes end-to-end in staging and document run time and observed side-effects
Affected tenants experience < 2% error rate within 30 minutes of traffic siphon start
KV reconciliation tooling shows < 1s median key fetch variance across replicas
Emergency throttle patch merged and can be toggled via console feature flag
Customer-facing template approved by support and sent to top 10 impacted tenants where applicable
steps: Identify degraded relay nodes via regional-error dashboard (dashboards/redwood/regional-relay-errors)
Open incident channel #inc-regional-relay and post initial triage summary with affected tenant list
Invoke controlled traffic siphon: update routing policy to apply 'siphon' tag to affected relays (console toggle or API call) to reduce new sessions by 80%
Run KV divergence check: execute kv-heal diagnostic against the affected relay group (tooling: /tools/kv-heal.sh) and collect diff report
If KV diffs > threshold, perform targeted KV reconcile using snapshot-and-replay method on replicas (follow safety checklist in runbook)
Monitor resource utilization and queue depths on warm standbys for 15 minutes post-siphon; scale up if sustained >70% GPU utilization
After KV aligns and errors fall below 2%, gradually shift traffic back in 10% steps over 20 minutes while monitoring SLOs
Close incident channel and convert notes to postmortem template; notify support with curated customer impact summary
rollback_plan: If errors spike or latency degrades > 30% after any step, immediately revert routing policy to previous state using console rollback button
If KV reconciliation introduces regressions, abort replay and restore from pre-reconcile snapshot (snapshots stored in s3://redwood-kv-snapshots/)
If warm standbys approach OOM or GPU faults, evacuate traffic to fallback region (predefined fallback set) and open escalation to infra oncall
Document all rollback actions in incident channel and attach timeline to ticket
notes: Tradeoff: aggressive siphon reduces immediate customer errors but increases load on fallback regions — mitigated by staging throttle and autoscale rules
Decision: use targeted KV replay for only affected tenant shards to minimize blast radius rather than full cluster rebuild
Follow-up: add continuous KV divergence metric and alert (ENG-76400) to detect issues preemptively
